teams.heading: Koli Sewabu says Fiji will follow Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch closely
teams.body: Fiji Rugby's Koli Sewabu said earlier this week that the union is following Mark Nawaqanitawase's possible switch of allegiance closely, after the winger's agent said he was weighing up his options. He is eligible for Fiji and Italy after a three-year stand-down, and the last of his 11 Test caps for the Wallabies came at the 2023 Rugby World Cup. Sewabu says Fiji would have genuine interest. Wallabies coach Les Kiss says he will wait until the end of the year to see where the player sits.

lead.why: A Fiji-side story with a named FRU official, and it is not a repeat of the Jake White coverage already on this tab.

teams.heading: England women's 41-match unbeaten run ends as Canada edge Red Roses 24-21
teams.body: England women's Red Roses lost their unbeaten streak in Toronto, Canada beating them 24-21 with a late Shoshanah Seumanutafa try three minutes from time. The 41-match run, stretching back almost four years, ended in the WXV Global Series, and Canada are the first side to beat England since November 2022. John Mitchell said: "I know this group has got more in them." Next up is the rematch in Ottawa.

lead.why: The biggest new England story in today's coverage, and the women's result is the one a fan would text about; the men's options are either already reported or not about England's senior side.

teams.heading: Thibaud Flament faces several weeks out with shoulder injury before Springboks test
teams.body: Les Bleus have lost another second-row option. Toulouse lock Thibaud Flament is facing several weeks on the sidelines with a shoulder injury, according to L'Équipe. The 29-year-old was tipped to pair up in the second row for the Tests against Fiji, the Springboks and Argentina, and Emmanuel Meafou is already expected to miss out with a knee injury. Fabien Galthié is now short of engine-room options before the Springboks test in Paris, against a world champion pack.

lead.why: It is a men's senior France story about a key second-row injury ahead of the Springboks test, and it is not a repeat of the stories already run this week.

teams.heading: Kitshoff backs Etzebeth's claim Irish acted arrogantly after 2023 Dublin match
teams.body: Steven Kitshoff, promoting his memoir Kitsie, has backed Eben Etzebeth's claim that the Irish reacted arrogantly towards the Springboks after the 2023 World Cup pool match in Dublin. The retired prop also recalls South Africa's rivalry with Ireland flaring after a 2017 loss in Dublin, and says the Springboks tend to make slights "extremely personal". It is a reminder that the grudge runs both ways, and that Ireland's meetings with South Africa carry memories on both sides.

lead.why: It is the only national men's item in today's pack, and it puts Ireland's conduct at the centre of a Springbok rivalry story.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa at home in November 2025
teams.body: South Africa are Italy's next opponent, in Round 4 of the Nations Championship, and the last meeting between the sides ended 32-14 to the Springboks. That was an International Friendlies match at home in November 2025, a single result rather than a wider record. Italy have lost all three Nations Championship matches so far, scoring 37 points and conceding 131.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham returns for Edinburgh against European giants, with a Scotland chance
teams.body: Darcy Graham is back playing for Edinburgh against European opposition, and MSN reports the return gives him a Scotland chance. The headline calls it a miracle, a word that tells you how much a fit Graham is worth to Scotland's wide options. With New Zealand arriving for Scotland's next test, every minute he gets for Edinburgh now doubles as an audition for the wing berths that matter most.

teams.heading: Louis Rees-Zammit keeps up push to end artificial Premiership pitches
teams.body: Louis Rees-Zammit is still pressing for an end to artificial pitches in the Premiership, after leg burns he suffered at Saracens. The BBC, the Guardian and SA Rugby Magazine have all carried the demand, and newer coverage repeats it, one headline quoting him: 'Can we please stop' playing on artificial surfaces. No formal decision from Premiership Rugby on the future of artificial surfaces has been reported. For Wales, the issue reaches well beyond one winger, with a growing list of Welsh internationals now playing in the Prem.

teams.heading: Argentina lead four-nation South American bid to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: Argentina are one of four South American nations, alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, who have submitted a joint bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, News24 reported in early October. Planet Rugby frames the bid as a challenge to World Rugby's desire for a European return, while another report, from Yahoo Sports, names Spain as front-runner. World Rugby has yet to announce a successful bid, so the decision remains open.

teams.heading: Les Kiss says Wallabies' first-half display 'not acceptable' after 43-21 Bledisloe defeat
teams.body: Les Kiss was scathing about the Wallabies' first half in the second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 defeat to the All Blacks at Accor Stadium in Sydney. "It's just not acceptable what was put out there," the coach said, stressing that the team must stop making the errors that cost them early. The loss was the Wallabies' 13th straight to New Zealand and came a week after a 50-19 defeat at Eden Park. Harry Wilson said the group had to start better.

lead.why: A coach's on-record verdict on the Bledisloe loss, a men's story not yet covered in the edition's recent run.

teams.heading: Japan score 309 and concede 308 in their last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308, averages of 28.1 and 28 a game. The biggest win inside that window was a 63-14 home victory over USA in September's Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Their current log shows one win from three, with a points difference of -26, and Wales are next up.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie expects Roigard TMO call to feature at World Rugby meeting
teams.body: Dave Rennie expects the TMO's handling of Cam Roigard's try-save against Australia to be a talking point at the World Rugby meeting in London. Rennie believes officials got the call right, but asked what happens when a penalty try is at stake and whether the two minutes lost are ever won back. "I haven't got an answer for you now, but no doubt it will be discussed in a couple of weeks." The Roigard save kept the Wallabies' Declan Meredith from scoring in the 43-21 win in Sydney.

lead.why: A fresh coach-level story with a direct New Zealand stake: Rennie's concern over how the TMO handled a try-saving tackle by his own scrum-half.

teams.heading: Springboks stay top as All Blacks cut gap to 0.82 points
teams.body: South Africa still head the World Rugby rankings, with 93.09 points to New Zealand's 92.27 after the All Blacks' 43-21 win over Australia in Sydney. New Zealand gained 0.46 points from that result, cutting the gap to 0.82. Australia dropped a place to seventh, while Scotland moved up to sixth. The All Blacks also beat Australia 50-19 at Eden Park earlier in the Bledisloe series.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item on the shortlist and a national men's story, with South Africa's top spot at stake.
